source_text: Sed quoniam nos sermo commonuit de iudicio futuro et de retributione ac suppliciis peecatorum, secundum quod comminantur sanctae scripturae et ecclesiastica praedicatio continet, eo quod iudiei tempore ‘ignis aeternus- et -tenebrae exteriores- et “carcer- et -caminus- et alia his similia peccatoribus praeparata sint, videamus quid etiam de his sentiri. oporteat, Sed ut ad haec competenti ordine veniatur, prius mihi videtur de resurrectione sermo movendus, ut sciamus quid est illud quod vel ad supplieium vel ad requiem ac beatitudinem veniet; de quo et in aliis quidem libris, quos de resurrectione scripsimus, plenius disputavimus et quid nobis de hoc videretur ostendimus. Sed et nune propter consequentiam tractatus pauca inde repetere non videtur absurdum, maxime propter hoe quod offenduntur quidam in ecclesiastica fide, quod velut stulte et penitus insipienter de resurrectione credamus, praecipue haeretici, quibus hoc modo arbitror respondendum. Si confitentur etiam ipsi quia resurrectio sit mortuorum, respondeant nobis: quid est quod mortuum est, nonne corpus? Corporis ergo resurrectio fiet. Tum deinde dicant si utendum putant nobis esse corporibus aut non? Arbitror apostolo Paulo dicente quia “seminatur corpus animale, resurget corpus spiritale”, istos negare non posse quod ‘corpus resurgat vel quia in resurrectione corporibus utamur. Quid ergo? Si certum est quia corporibus nobis utendum sit, et ‘corpora’ ea, quae ceciderunt, ‘resurgere’ praedicantur (non enim proprie resurgere dicitur nisi id, quod ante ceciderit), null dubium est idcirco ea ‘resurgeres, ut his iterum ex resurrectione induamur. Alterum ergo haeret ex altero. Nam et si resurgunt corpora, sine dubio ad indumentum nostri resurgunt, et si necesse est nos esse in corporibus (sieut certe necesse est), non in alüs quam in nostris corporibus esse debemus. Quae si verum est quod resurgunt et :spiritaha- resurgunt, dubium non est quin abiecta corruptione et deposita mortalitate resurgere dicantur a mortuis; ahoquin vanum videbitur et superfluum resurgere quem a mortuis, ut iterum moriatur. Quod ita demum intellegi evidentius potest, si qui diligenter advertat, quae sit -animalis corporis- qualitas, quae in terram seminata ‘spiritalis corporis. reparet qualitatem. Ex -animali- namque “corpore- ipsa virtus resurrectionis et gratia ‘spiritale corpus’ educit, cum id ab -indigmitate- transmutat ad ‘gloriam”. 2. Quoniam ergo haeretici eruditissimi sibi videntur et sapientissimi, interrogabimus eos, si omne corpus schema aliquod habet, id est aliquo habitu deformetur. Et si quidem dixerint esse corpus quod non aliquo habitu deformetur, imperitissimi omnium atque insipientissimi videbuntur. Nullus enim hoc negabit, nisi sit ab omni eruditione penitus alienus. Si vero secundum id, quod consequens est, dixerint quia omne corpus certo quo habitu deformatur, requiremus ab eis, si possunt nobis ‘spiritalis corporis’ habitum demonstrare atque deseribere; quod utique facere nullo modo poterunt. Sed et differentias eorum, qui resurgunt, inquiremus ab eis. Quomodo ostendent verum esse illud, quod dietum est quia “ala caro volucrum, alia piscium; et corpora caelestia et corpora terrestria; sed alia quidem caelestium gloria, alia vero terrestrium, alia gloria solis, alia gloria lunae, alia gloria stellarum, stella enim ab stella differt in gloria; ita et resurrectio mortuorum”? Secundum istam ergo consequentiam caelestium corporum ostendant nobis differentias gloriae eorum qui resurgunt, et si ullo genere conati fuerint secundum caelestium corporum differentias aliquam excogitare rationem, quaeremus ab eis, ut etiam secundum terrenorum corporum comparationem differentias resurreetionis adsignent. Nos vero ita intellegimus, quod volens apostolus describere, quanta esset differentia eorum, qui resurgent “in gloria, id est sanctorum, comparationem caelestium corporum sumpsit dicens: “Alia gloria solis, alia gloria lunae, alia gloria stellarume. Et iterum volens differentias eorum docere, qui in hae vita non expurgati ad resurrectionem venient, id est peccatores, de terrenis sumit exemplum dicens: “Alia caro volucrum, alia piscium”. Digne etenim sanctis caelestia, terrena peccatoribus comparantur. Haee quidem dicta sint adversum eos, qui “resurrectionem mortuorume, id est resurrectionem corporum negant. 3. Nune vero sermonem convertimus ad nonnullos nostrorum, qui vel pro intelleetus exiguitate vel explanationis inopia valde vilem et abiectum sensum de resurrectione corporis introducunt. (Quos interrogamus, quomodo intellegant ‘animale corpus- gratia resurrectionis immutandum et “spiritale- futurum, et quomodo quod ‘in infirmitate seminatur-. resurrecturum sentiant ‘in virtutes, et quod ‘in ignobilitate-, quomodo -resurgat in gloria; et quod ‘in eorruptione., quomodo ad “neorruptionem- transferatur. Quod utique si credunt apostolo quia corpus ‘in gloria et in virtute et in incorruptibilitate- resurgens, ‘spiritale” iam effectum sit, absurdum videtur et contra apostoli sensum dicere, id rursum ‘carnis et sanguinis- passionibus implicari, cum manifeste dieat apostolus: “Quoniam caro et sanguis regnum dei non possidebunt, neque corruptio incorruptionem possidebit”, Sed et illud quomodo aecipiunt, quod dicit apostolus quia “omnes autem immutabimur”? Quae utique immutatio secundum illum ordinem, quem superius diximus, expectanda est, in qua sine dubio dignum aliquid divina gratia sperare nos convenit; quod futurum credimus hoc ordine quo “nudum granum frumenti aut alicuius ceterorum” in terra seminatum describit apostolus, eui “deus dat corpus prout voluit”, cum prius "granum- ipsum “frumenti- -mortuum fuerit. Ita namque etiam nostra corpora velut “granum- cadere in terram putanda sunt; quibus insita ratio ea, quae substantiam continet corporalem, quamvis emortua fuerint corpora et corrupta atque dispersa, verbo tamen dei ratio illa ipsa, quae semper in substantia corporis salva est, erigat ea de terra et restituat ac reparet, sicut ea virtus, quae inest in grano frumenti, post corruptionem eius ac mortem reparat ac restituit granum in culmi corpus et spicae.- Et ita his quidem, qui regni eaelorum hereditatem consequi merebuntur, ratio illa reparandi corporis, quam supra diximus, dei iussu ex terreno et ‘animali corpore- “corpus- reparat ‘spiritale”, quod habitare possit in caelis; his vero, qui inferioris meriti fuerint vel abiectioris aut etiam ultimi et abstrusi, pro uniuscuiusque vitae atque animae dignitate etiam gloria corporis et dignitas dabitur: ita tamen ut etiam eorum, qui ad ‘ignem aeternum- vel ad ‘supplieia” destinandi sunt, per ipsam resurrectionis permutationem ita corpus incorruptum sit quod resurgit, ut ne suppliciis quidem corrumpi valeat ae dissolvi. 4. Si ergo ita se habet qualitas eius corporis, quod resurget a mortuis, videamus nunc quid sibi velit ‘ignis aeterni- comminatio. 4. Invenimus namque in Esaia propheta designari uniuscuiusque proprium esse ‘ignem’ quo punitur; ait enim: “Ambulate in lumine ignis vestri et in flamma, quam accendistis vobismet ipsis”. Per quos sermones hoc videtur indicari, quod unusquisque peccatorum “flammam-” sibi ipse proprii ‘ignis’ ‘accendat”, et non in aliquem ignem, qui antea lam fuerit accensus ab alio vel ante ipsum substiterit, demergatur. Cuius ignis esca atque materia sunt nostra peccata, quae ab apostolo Paulo ‘ligna et faenum et stipula- nominantur. Et arbitror quod sicut in corpore escae abundantia et qualitas vel quantitas cibi contraria febres generat, et febres diversi vel modi vel temporis secundum eam mensuram, qua intemperies collecta materiam suggesserit ac fomitem febrium (quae materiae qualitas, ex diversa intemperie congregata, causa vel acerbioris morbi vel prolixioris existit): ita anima cum multitudinem malorum operum et abundantiam in se congregaverit peccatorum, conpetenti tempore omnis illa malorum congregatio effervescit ad supplicium atque inflammatur ad poenas; cum etiam mens ipsa vel conscientia per divinam virtutem omnia in memorlam recipiens, quorum in semet signa quaedam ac formas, cum peccaret, expresserat, et singulorum, quae vel foede ac turpiter gesserat vel etiam impie commiserat, historiam quandam scelerum suorum ante oculos videbit expositam: tunc et ipsa conscientia propriis stimulis agitatur atque conpungitur et sui ipsa efficitur accusatrix et testis. Quod ita sensisse etiam Paulum apostolum puto cum dicit: “Inter se invicem cogitationibus aceusantibus aut etiam defendentibus in die, quo iudicabit deus oceulta hominum secundum evangelium meum per lesum Christum”. Ex quo intellegitur quod cirea ipsam animae substantiam tormenta quaedam ex ipsis peecatorum noxiis affectibus generantur. 5. Et ne satis tibi difficilis huius rei intellectus appareat, considerari possibile est ex his passionum vitis, quae animabus accidere solent, id est cum vel flammis amoris exuritur anima vel zeli aut livoris ignibus maceratur, aut cum irae agitatur insania vel tristitiae inmensitate consumitur, quomodo horum malorum nimietates aliquanti intolerabiliter ferentes, mortem subire quam huiuscemodi cruciatus perpeti tolerabilius habuere. Requires sane si his, qui vitiorum malis istis, quae supra diximus, inretiti sunt nec emendationis aliquid in hac vita adhue positi comparare sibimet potuerunt et ita ex hoc mundo abscesserunt, sufficiat illis ad poenam quod illis ipsis perdurantibus in se noxus affectibus eruciantur, id est irae vel furoris vel insaniae vel maeroris, quorum utique mortiferum virus nullo in hae vita emendationis medicamento mitigatum est; an his affectibus immutatis generalis poenae stimulis vexabuntur. Sed et aliam suppliciorum speciem intellegi arbitror posse, quia sicut quidem sentimus soluta corporis membra atque a suis invicem divulsa conpagibus inmensi doloris generare cruciatum, ita cum anima extra ordinem atque conpagem vel eam harmoniam, qua ad bene agendum et utihter sentiendum a deo creata est, fuerit inventa nec sibimet ipsi rationabilium motuum conpagine consonare, poenam cruciatumque putanda sit suimet ipsius ferre discidnu, et inconstantiae suae atque inordinationis sentire supplicium. Quae animae dissolutio atque divulsio cum adhibiti ignis ratione fuerit explorata, sine dubio ad firmiorem sui eonpagem instaurationemque solidatur. 6. Multa sunt etiam alia quae nos latent, quae illi soli cognita sunt, qui est medicus animarum nostrarum. Si enim ad corporis sanitatem pro his vitus, quae per escam potumque collegimus, necessariam habemus interdum austerioris ac mordacioris medicamenti curam, nonnumquam vero, si id viti qualitas depoposcerit, rigore ferri et sectionis asperitate indigemus, quodsi et haec supergressus fuerit morbi modus, ad ultimum conceptum vitium etiam ignis exurit: quanto magis intellegendum est medicum nostrum deum volentem diluere vitia animarum nostrarum, quae ex peccatorum et scelerum diversitate collegerant, uti huiuscemodi poenalibus curis, insuper etiam ignis inferre supplicium his, qui sanitatem animae perdiderunt? Cuius rei imagines etiam in scripturis sanctis referuntur. Denique in Deuteronomio sermo divinus peccatoribus comminatur quod ‘“febribus et frigoribus et aurugine- puniantur, et ‘oculorum vacillationibus et mentis alienatione et paraplexia et caecitate ac debilitate renium- cruclandi sint. Si qui ergo ex otio de omni scriptura congreget omnes languorum commemorationes, quae in comminatione peccatoribus velut corporearum aegritudinum appellationibus memorantur, inveniet quod animarum vel vitia vel supplicia per haec figuraliter indicentur. Ut autem intellegamus quia ea ratione, qua medici adiutoria languentibus adhibent, ut per curas reparent sanitatem, etiam deus agit circa eos, qui lapsi sunt et deciderunt in peccata, indicio est illud, quod per Hieremiam prophetam iubetur ‘calix furoris’ del ‘propinari omnibus gentibus. ut ‘bibant et insaniant et evomant”. In quo comminatur dicens quia si qui “noluerit bibere, non mundabitur. Ex quo utique intellegitur quod furor vindictae dei ad purgationem proficiat animarum. Quoniam autem et ea poena, quae per ignem inferri dicitur, pro adiutorio intellegitur adhiberi, Esaias docet, qui de Israhel quidem sie dicit: “Abluet dominus sordes filiorum et filiarum Sion, et sanguinem expurgabit e medio ipsorum spiritu iudicii et spiritu adustionise. De Chaldaeis autem sic dicit: “Habes carbones ignis, sede super eos, hi erunt tibi adiutorio”, et in alis dicit: “Sanctificabit eos dominus in igne ardentie, et in Malachia propheta ita dicit: “Sedens dominus conflabit sicut aurum et argentum populum suum, conflabit et purgabit et fundet purgatos filios Iuda”. 7. Sed et illud, quod de dispensatoribus non bonis in evangelio dietum est, qui “dividendi- dicuntur, et ‘pars eorum cum infidelibus poni-, tamquam ea pars, quae ipsorum propria non sit, aliorsum sit mittenda, sine dubio genus aliquod indicat poenae eorum, quorum, ut mihi videtur, separandus ab anima spiritus indicatur. Qui spiritus si quidem divinae naturae, id est spiritus sanctus intellegendus est, sentiemus hoe dictum de dono spiritus sancti; quod sive per baptismum sive per gratiam spiritus, cum alicui ‘sermo sapientiae- vel “sermo scientiae- vel alterius euiusque datus est dono et non recte administratus, id est aut ‘in terramdefossus est aut ‘in sudario- conhgatus, auferetur profecto ab anima donum spiritus, et “pars- reliqua quae superest, id est animae substantia, eum infidelibus- ponetur, divisa ac separata ab eo spiritu, cum quo “adiungens se domino unus spiritus esse- debuerat. Si vero hoc non de dei spiritu, sed de natura ipsius animae intellegendum est, pars eius melior illa dicetur, quae “ad imaginem- dei similitudinem- facta est, alia autem ‘pars’ ea, quae postmodum per liberi arbitrii lapsum. contra naturam primae conditionis et puritatis adsumpta est, quae utique pars utpote amica et cara materie corporalis “cum infidelium- sorte multatur. Potest autem etiam tertio sensu illud intellegi de divisione ista, ut quoniam unicuique fidelium, etiamsi “minimus sit in ecelesia’, adesse angelus dieitur, qui et ‘semper videre faciem dei patris- a salvatore perhibetur, et hie, qui utique unum erat cum eo, cui praeerat, siis per inoboedientiam efficiatur indignus, auferri ab eo dei angelus dicatur, et tune ‘pars eius-, id est humanae naturae pars, avulsa a dei parte “cum infidelibus’ deputetur, quoniam commonitiones appositi sibi a deo angeli non fideliter custodivit. S.
pass_a_gloss: But since our discourse has reminded us of the future judgment and the retribution and punishments of sins, according to what the holy scriptures and ecclesiastical preaching contain, because in the time of judgment 'eternal fire' and 'outer darkness' and 'prison' and 'furnace' and other things similar to these have been prepared for sinners, let us see what should be thought about these things. But in order to come to these things in a suitable order, it seems to me that the discourse about resurrection should be moved first, so that we may know what it is that comes either to punishment or to rest and beatitude; about which we have also discussed more fully in other books, which we have written about resurrection, and have shown what seems to us about this. But even now, because of the sequence of the treatise, it does not seem absurd to repeat a few things from that, especially because some people are offended in the ecclesiastical faith, that we believe in resurrection in a foolish and completely foolish way, especially heretics, to whom I think we should respond in this way. If they confess that there is a resurrection of the dead, let them answer us: what is it that has died, is it not the body? Therefore, the resurrection of the body will occur.

bible_refs.note: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God

pass_b_english: Since our discourse has reminded us of the future judgment, retribution, and the punishments of sins, just as the holy scriptures threaten and ecclesiastical preaching contains, and because at the time of judgment "eternal fire" and "outer darkness" and "prison" and "furnace" and other things like these have been prepared for sinners, let us see what we ought to think about these as well.

But so that we may approach these matters in a fitting order, it seems to me that we should first turn our discourse to the resurrection, that we may know what it is that will come either to punishment or to rest and blessedness; about this we have also disputed more fully in other books which we wrote on the resurrection, and we have shown what seemed right to us. Yet even now, on account of the sequence of this treatise, it does not seem absurd to repeat a few things from them, especially because some take offense at the ecclesiastical faith, supposing that we believe in the resurrection foolishly and utterly without wisdom—particularly heretics, to whom I think we ought to respond in this manner.

If they themselves confess that there is a resurrection of the dead, let them answer us: what is it that has died, is it not the body? Therefore the resurrection of the body will take place. Then let them say whether they think we ought to make use of bodies or not. I suppose that with the apostle Paul saying, "It is sown an animal body, it is raised a spiritual body" (1 Corinthians 15:44), they cannot deny that the body rises or that we shall make use of bodies in the resurrection. What then? If it is certain that we are to make use of bodies, and those bodies which have fallen are proclaimed to "rise" (for nothing is properly said to rise except what has fallen before), there is no doubt that they rise for this very purpose, that we may be clothed with them again through the resurrection.

One point follows from the other. For if bodies rise, beyond doubt they rise for our clothing; and if we must be in bodies (as we certainly must), we ought to be in no other bodies than our own. Now if it is true that they rise and rise "spiritual" (1 Corinthians 15:44), there is no doubt that they are said to rise from the dead with corruption cast off and mortality laid aside; otherwise it would seem empty and superfluous to rise from the dead only to die again. This can be understood even more clearly if one carefully considers what the quality of the "animal body" is, which, sown in the earth, restores the quality of the "spiritual body". For from the "animal body" the very power of the resurrection and grace bring forth the "spiritual body", when it is transformed from "dishonor" to "glory".

Because, then, the heretics consider themselves most learned and most wise, we will question them: if every body has some schema, that is, if it is formed by some habit. And if they should say there is a body which is not formed by any habit, they will appear the most unlearned and most foolish of all. For no one will deny this, unless he is entirely alien from all learning. But if, according to what follows, they say that every body is certainly formed by some habit, we will require of them whether they can demonstrate and describe the habit of the "spiritual body"; which they certainly will not be able to do in any way. We will also inquire from them about the differences among those who rise. How will they show to be true that which was said: "One flesh of birds, another of fish; and heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but one glory of the heavenly, another of the earthly; one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory; so also is the resurrection of the dead"?

According to this consequence, then, let them show us the differences of glory of the heavenly bodies of those who rise; and if they should attempt in any way to devise some reasoning according to the differences of heavenly bodies, we will ask them to assign the differences of the resurrection also by comparison with earthly bodies. We, however, understand it thus: the apostle, wishing to describe how great the difference would be of those who rise "in glory," that is, the saints, took the comparison of heavenly bodies, saying: "One glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, another glory of the stars." And again, wishing to teach the differences of those who come to the resurrection unpurged in this life, that is, sinners, he takes an example from earthly things, saying: "One flesh of birds, another of fish." Fittingly are heavenly things compared to the saints, earthly things to sinners. These things have been said against those who deny the "resurrection of the dead," that is, the resurrection of bodies.

Now, however, we turn our discourse to some of our own, who, whether from poverty of understanding or lack of explanation, introduce a very base and abject sense of the resurrection of the body. We ask them how they understand the "animal body" to be changed by the grace of the resurrection and to become "spiritual," and how they think that what is "sown in weakness" will rise "in power," and what is "sown in dishonor," how it will "rise in glory," and what is "sown in corruption," how it will be transferred to "incorruption." Surely if they believe the apostle that the body, rising "in glory and in power and in incorruptibility," has become "spiritual," it seems absurd and contrary to the apostle's sense to say that it is again implicated in the passions of "flesh and blood," when the apostle plainly says: "For flesh and blood cannot possess the kingdom of God, neither does corruption possess incorruption" (1 Corinthians 15:50). And how do they receive that which the apostle says: "We shall all be changed"? Which change is to be awaited according to that order which we spoke of above, in which it is fitting for us to hope for something worthy by divine grace; which we believe will happen in that order whereby the apostle describes a "naked grain of wheat or of some other" sown in the earth, to which "God gives a body as he willed," after the "grain" itself of "wheat" has first "died." Just so also our bodies are to be thought of as "grain" falling into the earth; in which there is implanted that principle which contains the bodily substance, which, though the bodies have died and been corrupted and dispersed, yet by the word of God that same principle which is always preserved in the bodily substance raises them from the earth and restores and repairs them, just as that power which exists in the grain of wheat, after its corruption and death, repairs and restores the grain into the body of the stalk and the ear.

And thus for those who will merit to obtain the inheritance of the heavenly kingdoms, that principle of repairing the body, which we spoke of above, by God's command repairs a "spiritual body" from an earthly and "animal body," which can dwell in the heavens; but for those who were of lesser merit or more abject or even last and hidden, according to the dignity of each one's life and soul, even the glory and dignity of the body will be given: yet in such a way that even for those who are destined for "eternal fire" or for "punishments," through the very exchange of the resurrection the body which rises is so incorruptible that it cannot be corrupted or dissolved even by punishments.
